Commentary.Commentary: Another one-sided affair ends. Zimbabwe continue to slip downhill, without showing any signs of getting up and putting up a fight. Pakistan, on the other hand, carry on with their dream run. It has been a complete mismatch so far. Things look gloomy for the hosts but they have one more opportunity to prove that they belong at this level. Join us for one final time on this tour on 22nd July at 0915 Local (0715 GMT). Till then, cheers!

Pakistan skipper, Sarfraz Ahmed says that Zaman and Imam played really well and he enjoyed their strokeplay. Mentions that it is a good thing that the top order is contributing heavily and also appreciates Asif Ali for his big-hitting prowess. Feels that Chigumbura and Tiripano batted well for Zimbabwe. States that their target was to bowl the opposition out under 160 and they executed their plans very well. Ends by saying that they will try their level best to win 5-0.

Man of the Match, Fakhar Zaman says that Imam-ul-Haq played really well and he got good support from him. Feels that this was his day and he is happy about scoring a double ton. States that their coach, Mickey Arthur wanted him to score a double ton if Pakistan won the toss and batted first. Mentions that it was a long day for him and he will get some treatment from the physio. Smiles and says that he will try not to give the middle order a chance even in the next game.

Zimbabwe skipper, Hamilton Masakadza says that it is not getting any easier for them. Mentions that they were never in the game. Credits Zaman for playing brilliantly and they found it tough to contain him. States that they were outplayed in all the three departments. Admits that a target of 400 is always difficult and they needed to play shots from the word go. Ends by saying that they will try to put in a better performance on Sunday.

After the domination by the Pakistan batsmen, their bowlers stepped up and cornered the Zimbabwean batsmen. It was a clinical bowling show with every bowler putting in his best and Shadab Khan with a 4-wicket haul stood out the most. Apart from the stand between Elton Chigumbura and Donald Tiripano, which in a way only delayed the inevitable, there was no resistance offered. Chasing 400 was never going to be easy and to be honest, no one expected them to do that either. But a little bit of fight would have done their confidence a world of good.

For a change, Pakistan changed the plot of this ODI. They chose to bat first and then posted their highest-ever score in ODIs. We witnessed plenty of records as Fakhar Zaman and Imam-ul-Haq raised the first-ever 300-plus stand for the opening wicket. The former also broke the 21-year old record by surpassing Saeed Anwar's 194 and becoming the first double centurion for Pakistan in this format.

Zimbabwe humbled again. Zimbabwe embarrassed again. Zimbabwe surrendered again. This has been the story of this bilateral series and the script remains the same. No fight presented by the African minnows. They are making it a habit of getting steamrolled. In a way, Fakhar Zaman alone has beaten Zimbabwe by 55 runs. In complete shambles, Zimbabwe. This is Pakistan's second biggest victory in ODIs (in terms of runs) and the biggest win ever in Bulawayo.

OUT! Given out lbw! Shadab finishes with a 4-wicket haul as PAKISTAN CRUSH ZIMBABWE BY 244 RUNS! A loopy ball around middle, turning back in, Ngarava tries working it across the line but misses. He is rapped on the pads, they appeal and the umpire agrees. The misery for Zimbabwe ends, their second biggest defeat in ODIs.
Flatter and shorter on middle, it's punched back from the crease.
Turning away sharply from around leg, Ngarava interestingly pads it away. Everyone is smiling. Even the umpires fail to hide their glee.
Tossed up ball on off, defended off the back foot.
Leans forward to a full ball and eases it down to long off for one.
Flatter and outside off, hit off the back foot to covers.

Spinning away from the batsman, Ngarava flashes and misses. Sarfraz behind the stumps collects it and smiles. He is very chirpy as we all know, this time in a comical mood. Comments that he will bowl and take the wicket.
Flatter and outside off, Ngarava goes hard at it and gets it away off the bottom edge.
Goes on the back foot and punches it down to long on for one.
Richard Ngarava is the last batsman.

OUT! Nine down. Malik also has a wicket. He lets out a loopy full ball around middle, from 'round the wicket, Chisoro clears his front leg to slog it over the leg side. But the ball catches the top edge and goes high up in the air. Usman Khan settles underneath it at long off and takes the skier safely. End is nigh.
Blessing Muzarabani is in next.

OUT! Drags it on! Khan delivers it short and outside off, a googly, Tiripano sticks back to punch it through the line but gets an inside edge onto the stumps. Tiripano's brief resistance is over. Shadab has his third wicket.
Full and flighted outside off, driven straight to the cover fielder.
Played to the point region by the batsman. No run.
FOUR! Easily done. Shadab serves this short around middle, a googly and it has been pulled with the spin through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Tickles it off his pads to the leg side, finds the gap and collects a single.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Powerplay 3 time!
Fails to connect properly with the reverse sweep, finds short third man.
The batsman has pushed it to the cover region.
Goes on the back foot and punches it back to the bowler.
Brings out the reverse sweep and gets it away off the bottom half of his bat. It speeds past short third man for a couple of runs.
Gets forward and pushes it with an angled bat to point.
Flighted on off, defended off the front foot.
Tendai Chisoro is the new batsman.

OUT! Trapped in front, no doubt about that. Shadab fetches a wicket by bowling a traditional leg spinning delivery. He drops it on a fuller length around off, Wellington is forward to defend but misses the ball completely. It curls back in a bit to hit him on the pads. Pretty dead in front and Zimbabwe continue with their slide.
Again the length is short and Tiripano slaps it to sweeper cover for one.
Shortish and outside off, punched off the back foot to point.

Dropped again by Sarfraz! A superb delivery, landing on middle and skidding away from the batsman. Tiripano is squared up in defense and gets a thick outside edge behind. Ahmed is once again late in reacting and it loops off his pads over the first slip fielder. A single taken. The Pakistan skipper is very chirpy behind the stumps, keeping an eye on every fielder and always passing on advice on how to field, where to stand etc. It appears he is not focusing on his own keeping duties much. These things become a habit and can cost a team in high-altitude games.
Full floated ball on off, pushed past the left side of the cover fielder for a run.
Flighted and on off, turning away, it's played off the back foot to point.
Shadab Khan is back on.
Tossed up and on off, Wellington draws forward and defends it watchfully.
Pushes this one flatter through the air, a little short and on middle, Tiripano moves back and helps it behind square leg for a run.
Slower through the air, full and on off, Masakadza pushes it down off the inner half of the blade to long on. A single taken.
Drags his length short and lands it wide outside off, it's been cracked off the back foot to deep cover-point for one.
Tossed up ball outside off, too wide and hence the batsman throws his bat at it. Hits it over the infield at covers and collects a couple of runs.
Flighted full ball on off, it's pushed off the front foot to covers.
Another one that pitches around the leg stump to go past Masakadza's flick to hit him on the pads. No appeal this time. A wicket and 2 runs from this over.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

Two Leg Byes! Fullish ball, pitching around leg and coming in. Masakadza tries to flick it away but misses to get hit on the pads. The ball rolls to the leg side as the batsmen set off. Ashraf starts appealing but bails out of it soon realizing it has pitched outside leg. Two runs taken in the end.
Time for Drinks! Meanwhile, Wellington Masakadza comes out to bat.

OUT! It is Faheem Ashraf who strikes for the second time! Good skills displayed by him to fox the batsman. He steams in from over the wicket and bowls a fullish delivery in the tight off stump corridor. After pitching, the ball skids off the surface and seams in as Chigumbura's bat comes down at an angle, failing to negate the inward shape. The ball goes on to thud into his back pad. Pakistan appeal in unison and up goes the umpire's finger. The 69-run association has been cut short, the only one for Zimbabwe which looked reliable.
Full length ball attacking the stumps, defended down the track.
Dug in short, Elton ducks under it.
In line of the stumps, Chigumbura tries to drive it through covers but the ball rolls off the inside half of his bat past the bowler. A run taken.
Spinning in sharply, the wrong one, kept out just in the nick of time.
Half-tracker from Shah but not made full use of. The batsman pulls it to the man at deep mid-wicket for a run.
The wrong one from Yasir but it is slow through the air. Allows Tiripano to read it off the pitch as he blocks it down the track.
On a flatter trajectory, guided nicely to short third man.
Wide! Spinning down the leg side, going past Tiripano's attempted flick shot.
Well played! Tossed up outside off, Chigumbura strokes it nicely through extra cover. Asif Ali in the deep runs to his left to keep the ball in play. Saves a run for his side.
Outside off, defended towards backward point.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.

FOUR! Close shave! Another effort ball from Ashraf, rising on Tiripano. He is in an uncomfortable position but still goes for the pull. Only gets a glove on it as the ball goes behind. Sarfraz leaps to his left but it goes past him in a jiffy and through to the fence. With that, the highest partnership for the hosts comes up in this series. Donald has decided to get a move on.
Another bouncer, Donald ducks underneath it.
Short ball around off, Tiripano commits himself to the pull again but only connects with thin air. He was probably beaten for pace there.
In the channel outside off, the batsman waits for it and dabs it towards the point region.
Spinning away, tapped with an open bat face past point for a run.
FOUR! Poor delivery and it gets the treatment! Half-tracker, Tiripano stands tall and nails the pull over mid-wicket to find the fence.

Loopy delivery around off, Tiripano goes for the fancy reverse sweep but gets a glove on it. The fielder at first slip dives to his right but the ball falls short of him and goes past as well. Normally, Donald plays that shot well.
Sits back in the crease and forces it to covers.
Slower through the air, Donald pushes at it but gets an edge past first slip.
Fullish ball on middle, eased through mid on for a single.
Straying on the pads, flicked to deep square leg for a run.
Back of a length ball, skids through after pitching. Elton is hurried by it as he manages to defend it to covers.
Chigumbura shuffles a bit to counter the inward angle on this length ball and flicks it to mid-wicket.
Once again a delivery in the same corridor, glided successful to third man to rotate strike.
Tiripano tries to guide a similar ball past short third man but finds him.
Short of a length well outside off, guided past point for a single.
Faheem Ashraf is back on.

Spinning in, tucked through mid-wicket for a run. That brings up the 50-run stand for the duo. This has brought some respectability for them. Zimbabwe have had only 1 fifty partnership in this series before.
Once again Chigumbura leans forward and plays this one with the spin to the same region.
Gets forward to the pitch of the ball to tap it to covers.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Almost, almost! Sliding in at a good pace, Chigumbura tries to cut it through point but only manages a bottom edge. He is lucky as the ball deflected onto his pads. Otherwise, he was in trouble.
Quick and full, jammed back to the bowler.
Outside off, this time Tiripano can't get it past point.
Good running!  Shortish ball outside off, dabbed past the left side of the point fielder. The third man fielder runs to his right and by the time he cuts it off, two runs are taken.
Wide!  Junaid tries to hurry Donald with a short one but it is well-directed. Down the leg side as the batsman ducks to it.
Similar length ball in line of the stumps, pulled away with the angle to deep mid-wicket. A run taken.
Shortish ball, rising on the batsman. He hops and steers it to third man for a run.
A harmless length ball outside off, Tiripano allows it to go through.
Back of a length outside off, pushed off the back foot to deep cover. A run taken.
Leans ahead to this one to dead-bat it.
Comes forward again and keeps it out.
Tossed up ball, Donald comes forward and blocks it solidly.
Pushes this one down to long off for a run. So, Zimbabwe avoid the ignominy of the heaviest defeat in ODIs. Ireland had lost to New Zealand in 2008 by a margin of 290.
Driven through the covers by the batsman. They manage to come back for the second.
The googly from Yasir, Elton leans ahead to defend it.
Angling in sharply, tucked through mid-wicket for a run.
Streaky! Back of a length ball, angling in, Elton pushes at it but gets an inside edge that goes towards square leg. A couple taken.

In the air... but safe! Well-directed short ball in line of the stumps, Donald goes for the pull but only manages a top edge towards fine leg. The fielder runs in but the ball lands down safely before reaching him. A run taken.
Low full toss outside off, Tiripano plays it gently towards covers. Could have hit it anywhere.
Khan drags his length back as Tiripano stays back to stonewall it.
Full length ball attacking the stumps, Donald keeps it out nicely.
Double change as Junaid Khan is back.
Edged but safe! Spinning in nicely, Elton is early into his clip and hence, gets a leading edge but it lands safely on the off side.
Tossed up delivery, defended solidly off the front foot.
Fullish delivery, kept out watchfully.
Shorter in length, crunched away with the spin to deep cover for a single.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Stays back to play this with an angled bat to point.
Yasir Shah returns for a bowl.

SIX! What a hit! Wrong one on middle and off, Chigumbura reads it correctly, clears his front leg and smokes it over mid-wicket. It is going, going and sails into the stands. The 100 comes up for Zimbabwe. A good over for the hosts, 12 from it.
Played with the spin to the point region.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. One run added to the total.

Dropped and FOUR! That should have been taken. Perhaps, Sarfraz was not concentrating well. Spinning away from Tiripano as he attempts to drive it but gets an outside edge. The keeper is late to react. The ball deflects off his gloves as Azam gets low to his left but it bounces in front of him and goes past him to the fence.
Outside off, spinning away, left alone.
The wrong one outside off, Chigumbura picks it correctly and punches it through covers for a run.
Loopy ball, drifting in as well, played with the angle through mid on. A single taken.
Floated around off, Elton lunges in defense.
Played with the spin to the mid-wicket region.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. They pick up a single.

FOUR! A boundary after ages, something for the crowd to smile about. Shorter in length, Tiripano rocks back and cuts it through extra cover. The mid off fielder hares after it, tries his best but only comes second best.
Drifting in nicely, Donald strides ahead to block it with authority.
Similar length ball, defended from the comfort of the crease.
On a flatter trajectory, outside off, tapped through covers for a run.
Tossed up generously, defended solidly off the front foot.
Turn and bounce for Shadab! Pitches on off and shoots away, Donald goes for the cut but is late on it.
Fuller this time, eased through mid off for a run.
Shorter in length outside off, chopped towards point.
Slower through the air, played gently towards mid on.
Gets to the pitch of the tossed up ball to place it through mid on for a run.
The batsman drives the ball straight down the ground.
Spinning down leg, turned around the corner for a single.
Almost a replica of the previous delivery as the batsman plays the same shot.
Spinning in as Elton flicks it to mid-wicket.
Comes forward and defends it nicely.
Hangs back and punches this one for a run.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. The batsmen have run through for a single.

Howzat? The answers to that is No. Conventional leg spinner on middle and leg, spinning away. Chigumbura exposes his stumps and goes for the sweep but seems to have missed it to get hit on the pads. The ball goes towards fine leg as the batsmen set off. Shadab is confident but umpire Ian Gould turns it down. The bowler has a look at the square leg umpire, with a curious look on his face. Gould signals it as leg byes, three in the end. That was close.
Spinning away, Elton rocks back and cuts it with the spin to point.
On a flatter trajectory, kept out watchfully.
Spinning into Elton as he drives it through mid on for a run.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Elton makes good use of the depth of the crease to dead-bat the shorter delivery.
Leans ahead to the tossed up ball and taps it with the spin to mid-wicket.
Tiripano clears his front leg to this one and taps it through mid on to rotate strike.
Straighter one, in line of the stumps, pushed back to the bowler.
Shadab drags his length back this time, Donald forces it to sweeper cover for a run.
Pitched up this time, Tiripano lunges in defense.
Shorter in length again, defended solidly off the back foot.
On a flatter trajectory, hurries Tiripano slightly as he somehow jams it out down the track.
Donald strides ahead to this one and defends it with his bat and pad close together.
Loopy ball, around off, kept out watchfully.
Similar delivery, a similar shot from Tiripano as he places it to long on for a run. A decent first over from Malik.
Strides forward to the flighted ball and taps it through mid on for a single.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Slower through the air, eased off the front foot towards the cover region.
A touch wider this time, outside off, driven through mid off to rotate strike.
Starts off with a loopy ball, drifting in, milked towards long on for a single.
Shoaib Malik to roll his arm over now.
Leans ahead to this one and keeps it out. A wicket and a run off this over.
Donald Tiripano strides out to bat.

OUT! Another one bites the dust! Shadab bowls a tossed up delivery on middle and it is fullish in length, Moor clears his front leg and tries to tonk it down the ground against the spin. However, the connection is not that good as the ball flies over wide mid on. Junaid Khan in the deep runs in a bit and then goes across to his right to take a well-judged catch. Half the side back in the hut for the hosts now.
A bit shorter in length, punched off the back foot towards covers.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
This time the googly is a better executed one. Moor reads it nicely and taps it beside the pitch on the leg side.
Attempted googly again but the length is very full, Chigumbura knocks it down to long on to rotate strike.
Slightly overpitched outside off, Moor goes for a drive but doesn't time it that well. Finds the fielder at extra cover.
Tries to catch the batsman off guard with a full length ball attacking the stumps. Peter is up to it as he jams it back to Faheem.
Aggression from Ashraf as he bowls an effort ball. It rises up as Peter ducks under it nicely.
Ashraf opts to pitch this one up around off, Moor strides forward and plays it gently to mid off.

Tight run but good to see some urgency from the two. Similar length ball, tapped with an open bat face towards cover-point as the batsmen set off. The fielder there attacks the ball and has a shy at the striker's end but misses. Had it hit, it would have been close.
Back of a length ball, angling in, Elton covers the line and defends it stoutly.
A bit shorter in length, ample time for Chigumbura to rock back and cut it to sweeper cover. A run taken.
Stump-to-stump line, pushed towards mid on.
Driven through the covers by the batsman.

Was there an inside edge? Probably. Googly, spinning in at a quicker pace, Elton goes at it with hard hands but gets an inside edge onto his pads. The ball deflects off his pads behind. Ahmed is a bit late to react as the ball goes past him.
Fullish and floated up generously, defended solidly off the front foot.
Tossed up outside off, eased through wide mid off for a run.
Shadab Khan comes into the attack.

Drinks break. It has been all Pakistan since the time this series has begun. Nothing different today also. First with the bat they dominated and now their bowlers have cornered the Zimbabwean batsmen. When the match will end appears to be a more pertinent question at this point.
Identical to the last delivery. Once again Chigumbura is very sound and solid in his front foot defense.
Full and around off, Chigumbura draws forward and defends it close to his body.
Fullish and outside off, driven off the front foot to mid off.
Tries to work a length ball around but it takes the inner half of the bat and runs to long leg for one.
Back of a length ball on off, Moor is on the back foot as he defends it back.
Good length ball on middle, worked in front of square leg for a run.
Sliding down the leg side, helped towards square leg for a single.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. No run.
Leans forward and pushes it with the spin through cover-point for a single.
Moor has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

Yasir gives it plenty of flight. The ball almost hangs in the air for a while before landing on a fuller length outside off. Moor drives but finds the cover fielder again. With the batsman not looking to attack, it becomes easy for a spinner to give flight.
Full and flighted outside off, driven straight to covers.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot. End of a successful over, a run and a wicket from it.
Lands it on a length outside off, Elton plays it off his back foot to point.
Elton Chigumbura is the new batsman with Zimbabwe just going through the motions.

OUT! Excellent low catch by Sarfraz Ahmed. Ashraf dishes out a full length ball just around off, maybe a hint of inward shape, or probably going on with the angle. Murray with a static footwork tries to drive through the line but it takes the inner half of his bat and goes behind to the keeper. Sarfraz does well to snap it inches above the surface. They appeal and the finger has gone up. Zimbabwe lose their fourth wicket and are going nowhere in this run chase. This is also the 7th catch in the series for the Pakistan skipper, the most by him is 10 against Sri Lanka in the Middle-East in 2017.
Angles in a length ball on off, Murray mistimes his drive to the cover fielder.
A back foot punch to sweeper cover for a single.
Shortish and on off, Moor taps it down to covers and his partner looks for a run. Immediately sent back.
Generously tossed up this time, full and drifting on middle, Moor knocks it down to long on for a single.
Tossed up and a little wide outside off, Murray rocks back and plays it square of the wicket on the off side for a run.
Nice flight this time. A googly around off, fuller in length, Murray gets forward to defend without reading the variation. Gets an inside edge onto his front pad.
A little short and on middle, not turning much, Murray turns it off his pads but finds mid-wicket.
Full flighted ball on off, it's driven down to long off for a single.
Flighted delivery on middle, punched back to the bowler.
Shortish and outside off, cut through backward point for one.

Nicely timed and placed on this occasion. A shortish ball outside off, Moor pushes it with an angled bat past the left side of the point fielder. By the time third man cuts it off, they take a couple of runs.
Back of a length delivery on off, Moor leans back a bit and then taps it down to point.
Stays on the back foot and forces it through covers for a run.
Bowls it short and wide outside off, Ryan cuts but finds the point fielder.
Starts with a length ball outside off, Moor pushes it past the cover fielder for a single.
Faheem Ashraf to bowl now. He is fresh from a five-wicket haul and will be looking to leave his impact once again.
Wrong 'un around middle, Moor picks it late and keeps it out towards mid-wicket.
Skidder again in this over, this time around off, Moor punches it off his back foot to long off for a single. 50 up for Zimbabwe, a little milestone for them!
Loopy and full on off, Moor drives it off his front foot towards the bowler.
Quicker one this time, probably a slider. It lands wide outside off and skids through, Moor watches the line closely and then lets it through.
Tossed up ball on off, this time Murray drives it past the left side of the bowler to long off. A single taken.
Full and flighted on off, driven firmly back to the bowler who made a half stop in his followthrough.
Powerplay 2 time! A maximum of 4 fielders are now allowed outside the circle until the 40th over. Just an FYI, Zimbabwe have not batted that long in this series so far.
Lands it full and on off, Moor covers the line and blocks it off his front foot.
Some chin music for the batsman, he lets that bouncer through to the wicketkeeper.

Smart thinking from the bowler. Although the execution wasn't accurate. He follows up the short delivery with a low full toss, Moor brings his bat down in time and gets it away off the thick inside edge. It rolls through square leg and they cross for a couple of runs.

Play and a miss! A sharp delivery, this time the length is short and it's outside off. Moor leans back and then tries to ramp it over the keeper's head at the last moment. Fails to get any wood behind it.
Another length ball is angled into the batsman, Moor is solid in his defense.
Usman Khan speeds in from around the wicket and angles in a length ball on off, Moor plays it from the back foot and pushes it towards mid off.
Flatter again, short and outside off, punched off the back foot to covers.
Sliding down the leg side, Murray tries to flick but misses.
Quicker and on off, stroked off the back foot to long off for one.
Goes on the back foot to a shortish ball again and punches it to covers.
Flatter this time, short and on off, it's been punched to long off for a single.
Flighted and full on off, Murray is on the front foot in defense but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Yasir Shah to bowl his leggies.
Back of a length ball on off, defended off the back foot to end the over.

Almost another wicket. Usman switches to 'round the wicket and bangs in a short ball on off. Moor initially looks to duck underneath it but after watching the ball come at him, he has to fend at it. Ends up getting it away off the shoulder of the bat and luckily for him, it falls short of the lone slip fielder. Travels past him to third man and they cross for a couple of times.
FOUR! Nice way to get off the mark, Moor. A length ball angling away from the batsman, Peter hits it off his front foot and it goes on one bounce past the diving point fielder for a boundary.
Khan bangs it in, Moor picked that bouncer early and let it through to the keeper.
Gets off the mark, Murray. This time he finds the gap wide of the point fielder after playing the square cut. The third man fielder cuts it off in the deep and they take a run.
Back of a length ball outside off, angling away from the batsman, Murray hits it square of the wicket on the off side but finds the point fielder.
Full in length and just around off, Moor is on the front foot as he presents a solid defensive shot. A wicket maiden for Junaid!
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump
Good length ball on off, Moor defends it off his back foot.
Peter Moor is the new batsman.

OUT! Junaid Khan hunts his 100th ODI victim! Becomes the 20th bowler for Pakistan to achieve this mark. A back of a length delivery angling into the batsman, around off, Hamilton remains back to swing it over mid-wicket. Uses his wrists to good effect to play that shot but fails to get the desired elevation. Ends up handing a simple catch to Babar Azam inside the ring. It appears that the procession has begun...
A good looking cover drive by Masakadza but he finds the fielder inside the ring.
Good length delivery outside off, Murray stands back to play it to point.
Murray has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Wide called for height! Another bounce by Usman, this time it goes well over the head of the batsman.
Ryan Murray is the next batsman.

OUT! Usman strikes again to pick his second wicket. He once again delivers a heavy ball, short in length and outside off, Musakanda could have played an upper cut to it but tries to pull it across the line. Fails to middle his shot properly and Faheem Ashram at mid on takes the simplest of catches. A sorry beginning for the home team yet again.
A little short in length this time, on middle, Hamilton drags his pull off the inside edge. It rolls wide of mid on for a run.
A length ball on middle, defended off the back foot.

Not quite from the meat of the bat. A length ball around middle and leg, Musakanda stays back to power it down the ground. It goes over mid on and Faheem Ashraf chases it down from the circle. Pulls it just before the rope and saves a run for his team.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Once again the Zimbabwean skipper plays a length ball from the crease but finds the point fielder.
Lands it on a length and outside off, played down from the crease to point.
Fuller and on off, pushed off the front foot to mid on.

SIX! Fantastic shot! Junaid is operating from 'round the wicket and Hamilton just uses his angle to his advantage. Gets down forward and across to paddle it all the way over fine leg for a maximum. The skipper is trying his best to stay positive.
Nearly drags it on! Fuller length ball outside off, Hamilton bottom edges his attempted drive through the line and it goes behind to the keeper. Sarfraz does well to stop it.
On a length and outside off, tapped wide of point for a single.
Full and angling in around off, once again it has been played down towards mid on. Went quickly to the fielder this time.
Knocks a full ball down towards mid on for one.

SIX! That appeared to have come off the top edge but sailed into the trees at fine leg. A biggie to open his account. Musakanda takes on the short ball, tries to wheel a pull shot but it finds the top edge and goes all the way.
Tarisai Musakanda is the new batsman at number 3.

OUT! A forgetful debut for Kamunhukamwe. Khan digs in a short ball around off, a pacey one to hurry up the batsman. Tarisai tries pulling it but fails to middle it. It balloons in the air off the top edge and Usman runs back to catch the ball easily. Pakistan draw first blood in the fourth over.
Play and a miss! Back of a length delivery outside off, angling away, Kamunhukamwe tries to play at it but fails to connect.
SIX! Fine shot! Masakadza has just picked the length delivery from around off and swings it all the way over long on for a biggie. Intentions are clear!
Around off on a length, blocked from the crease.
FOUR! A cracking pull shot by the Zimbabwean skipper. He picks up the short delivery early, goes deep inside the crease and pulls it powerfully to the deep square leg fence.
Shortish on off, punched straight to the cover fielder.
On a length and straighter in line, defended to mid-wicket.

Edgy! Back of a length delivery angling away from the debutant, Tinashe stays back to punch it through the line but it takes the outside edge and hurries past the first slip fielder to third man. A single taken.
Another front foot defensive shot offered by Masakadza.
Hamilton has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Lands it full and around middle, Masakadza plays it down the ground but straight towards mid on.
Fullish and on middle, it has been pushed across the line but straight to mid-wicket.

Huge cry for an lbw! Not given. Khan with a full length ball, Hamilton fails to work it across the line. He is rapped on the pads, they appeal but nothing from the umpire. The replays show that it pitched outside leg.
Slight issue with the sight screen. A little bit of gap spotted in between and the groundsmen are trying to close it.
Starts with a back of a length ball around leg, Kamunhukamwe tucks it in front of square leg and scampers across to the other end.
Usman Khan to begin proceedings from the other end with the second new ball. A slip in place.
FOUR! A good end to the first over for Zimbabwe! Masakadza is off the mark in style! Full and on off, Hamilton plants his front foot forward and hits it through mid off for a boundary.
Shortish outside off, TK slaps it towards cover-point. The fielder there does well to dive to his right and make a half stop. He can't stop a run though.
Hits the length hard on off, the batsman blocks it.
Back of a length on off, kept out.
BEATEN! Excellent stuff! Angles this from a length on off away from the right-hander. Kamunhukamwe pokes at it and gets beaten.

A huge appeal but not given! Action straightaway! An inswinger by Khan but is on the pads. Masakadza tries to flick but misses. The players appeal but the umpire shakes his head. Missing leg. The batsmen run a leg bye as the ball rolls towards square leg. Zimbabwe need another 399.

We are back for the chase! Out come the players along with the umpires. The debutant, Tinashe Kamunhukamwe and Hamilton Masakadza are the openers. The skipper will be on strike and he will face Junaid Khan. He is on 99 ODI wickets, can he get his 100th?
